_comment: Door-side configuration template. The deployment step rewrites the
placeholder values from the answers given in the wizard; nothing here is a
The four actuator fields below are null on purpose. ActuatorConfig fails to
construct while they are null, and that failure is the safety interlock: a
guessed relay_contact on a fail-safe magnetic lock leaves the door open
permanently, and a guessed active_high pulses the lock at boot. They must
come from a meter and a wiring check on the installed hardware.
facedb.signature_key is mandatory whenever facedb.url is plaintext http://.
Devices with a broken clock cannot validate TLS certificates, so on those
the integrity boundary moves up to the application layer: an HMAC-SHA256
signature over the canonical manifest. No key, no start.

camera._max_frame_age_note: The grabber thread keeps only the newest frame; the recogniser consumes at whatever rate face-rec-api answers. A frame older than this is dropped instead of recognised: opening the door on a three-second-old face opens it for whoever is standing there now, not for the person who was matched.

policy._threshold_note: 0.62 is a starting point, not a calibrated value. The design spec forbids treating the upstream default as a result: sweep positive and negative pairs on the installed camera and set it from that. No FAR/FRR figure exists for this project.

actuator._backend_note: sysfs drives /sys/class/gpio (bind-mounted into the container by the compose file). libgpiod drives /dev/gpiochipN instead and needs gpiochip + line below plus a --device passthrough; use it on kernels where the sysfs interface is gone.
actuator._takeover_note: allow_takeover stays false. The reCamera Pro survey found gpio131 already exported by another application; silently taking over a pin means either two processes fighting or driving something that is not the door relay. When a takeover is genuinely intended it is set explicitly and shows up in health().
